questions.question: Explain the trading stock surplus: its entry, why prudence permits it, and why it still warrants investigation.
questions.expected_answer: When the stocktake counts more than the books claim (R10 745 against R10 700), the books rise to the fact: debit Trading Stock R45, credit Trading Stock Surplus, an income. Prudence refuses hoped-for gains but not counted ones — the physical count is evidence in both directions. It still deserves suspicion because stock does not breed: a surplus means a record is wrong somewhere — a duplicated sale, an unrecorded receipt of goods — so the gain is booked and the cause investigated.

questions.question: Correct the three worked errors — advertising in Stationery (R320), the omitted R600 credit sale (cost R400), and wages entered as R2 070 instead of R2 700 — stating the discipline behind each correction.
questions.expected_answer: Wrong account: debit Advertising R320, credit Stationery R320 — move the amount between pockets; totals unchanged, detail now true. Omission: do the skipped entry in full — debit Debtors Control R600, credit Sales R600, plus debit Cost of Sales R400, credit Trading Stock R400. Wrong amount: top up by the difference only — debit Wages R630, credit Bank R630; never reverse and re-enter when a top-up will do. The discipline: name what happened, name what should have happened, journalise only the gap — with a narration. All three slipped past the trial balance and were caught by document checks and reconciliations.

questions.question: Describe the post-closing trial balance: what it contains, what it may never contain, and its double role in the cycle.
questions.expected_answer: After the closing transfers empty every nominal account (profit to Capital, Drawings settled against Capital), only the balance-sheet accounts survive: assets, liabilities and the updated Capital — the accounting equation itemised and proven level. It may never contain an income or expense: flows die at midnight, so any nominal account on the list is an error by definition. Its double role: it is this year's ending position and simultaneously next year's opening balances — the cycle closing into itself, which is why the cycle is a cycle.
